title: Bounded section defect under normalization of a generically reduced projective curve
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field] and let $X\subset\mathbf P^N_k$ be a connected generically reduced one-dimensional closed subscheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-projective-space-twist]. Here generically reduced means that the local ring at each generic point of an irreducible component is reduced. Let $D=X_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme], and let $\nu:\coprod_{i=1}^t E_i\longrightarrow D\longrightarrow X$ be the disjoint union of the normalizations of its reduced irreducible components [def-sc-normalization]. The list is finite, each $E_i$ is a smooth proper connected curve [def-sc-curves, def-weil-proper-morphism], and $\nu$ is finite. Put $A_i=\nu^*\mathcal O_X(1)|_{E_i}$ and $e_i=\deg_k A_i>0$ [def-pc-module-pullback, def-pc-degree-line-bundle]. For each $m\ge0$ put $H_m=H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(m))$ and $T_{i,m}=H^0(E_i,A_i^{\otimes m})$, with Zariski module cohomology [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. The canonical restriction and pullback map is
$$\rho_m:H_m\longrightarrow\bigoplus_{i=1}^t T_{i,m}.$$
There exist integers $C,m_0\ge0$, depending on this embedded scheme, such that for every $m\ge m_0$ all these spaces are finite-dimensional and
$$\dim_k\ker\rho_m\le C,\quad \dim_k\operatorname{coker}\rho_m\le C,\quad |\dim_k T_{i,m}-me_i|\le C\ (1\le i\le t),\quad |\dim_k H_m-m\sum_i e_i|\le C.$$
The constants need not be uniform as $X$ varies. No nodality, linear normality or absence of finite embedded nilpotents is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0BXR, lemma-normalization-locally-algebraic; 0C1R, lemma-prepare-delta-invariant; 0AYT, lemma-chi-tensor-finite. With coherent.tex Tag 0B3J (lemma-coherent-support-dimension-0) and curves.tex Tag 0BS6 (lemma-rr). Agent assembly including finite embedded nilpotents.

proof.text: Write $i:D\hookrightarrow X$, $E=\coprod_iE_i$, $p:E\to D$, and $L=\mathcal O_X(1)$. By [lem-pc-projective-proper] $X$ is proper; [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper](c) make $D$ proper as well. Apply [lem-trf-proper-field-invertible-coherent] to obtain Noetherianness and coherence of the structure sheaves. The component cover [lem-trf-proper-curve-normalized-component-cover] gives finitely many integral proper dimension-one components and their finite normalization cover. Its zero-dimensional components would be open and closed singletons, so connectedness and $\dim X=1$ exclude them. The reduction has the same space as $X$, hence has precisely these dimension-one components. Each $E_i$ is integral, hence connected. An algebraically closed field is perfect (every irreducible polynomial is linear), so [lem-sc-normalization-properties](c) makes every $E_i$ smooth. This proves the asserted geometric properties of the normalization.

source.place: Tag 0BXR (lemma-normalization-locally-algebraic); Tag 0B5Y (lemma-ampleness-in-terms-of-degrees-components), normalized component cover; morphisms.tex Tag 01WC (lemma-locally-projective-proper).

proof.text: The hyperplane bundle $L$ is invertible and ample by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-ample-invertible]. Its restriction to each reduced component is ample, and so is its pullback to $E_i$: both the component closed immersion and the finite normalization morphism are affine, by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] for the latter, and [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-ample-invertible] applies successively (a closed immersion is affine by its affine quotient description). Pullback and tensor products preserve invertibility by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor]. Thus [lem-trf-proper-integral-curve-ample-degree] gives the positive integer $e_i=\deg_kA_i$.

source.place: Tag 0892 (lemma-pullback-ample-tensor-relatively-ample), part (2); varieties.tex Tag 0B5X (lemma-ample-curve); properties.tex Tag 01PU (lemma-ample-on-closed).

proof.text: Let $J=\mathcal N_X$. The reduction definition gives $0\to J\to\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_D\to0$. It makes $J$ quasi-coherent; since $\mathcal O_X$ is coherent, [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth](2) makes $J$ coherent. At each component generic point $\eta$, generically reducedness and the reduction's quotient description give $J_\eta=0$. Here the nilradical commutes with passage to a stalk: a nilpotent germ has a representative whose power is zero after shrinking. For any point where $J_x=0$, choose finitely many local generators; each has zero germ and is zero on a smaller neighbourhood, so their finite intersection is a neighbourhood on which $J=0$. Thus $\operatorname{Supp}J$ is closed and misses every component generic point. Any irreducible closed subset of this support is properly contained in a component of $X$; a strict chain inside it of length one would then extend to length two in $X$. Therefore $\dim\operatorname{Supp}J\le0$.

source.place: Tag 01Y1 (lemma-coherent-Noetherian-quasi-coherent-sub-quotient); elementary finite-generator proof of closed support, as in Tag 01Y5 (lemma-coherent-support-closed).

proof.text: By [lem-trf-curve-normalization-coherent-support] on the reduced pure one-dimensional finite-type scheme $D$, there is an exact sequence $0\to\mathcal O_D\to p_*\mathcal O_E\to Q\to0$, with $Q$ coherent and supported on finitely many closed points. Put $L_D=i^*L$ and $J_m=J\otimes L^{\otimes m}$, $Q_m=Q\otimes L_D^{\otimes m}$. Applying [lem-pc-chi-zero-dim-support] on the proper schemes $X,D$ gives, for every $m\ge0$, $H^1(X,J_m)=0$, $h^0(X,J_m)=a:=h^0(X,J)$ and $h^0(D,Q_m)=b:=h^0(D,Q)$. Coherent cohomology finiteness [lem-pc-euler-characteristic-well-defined] shows that $a,b$ are finite nonnegative integers. All twists used here are invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor].

Tensor the reduction sequence by $L^{\otimes m}$ and the normalization sequence by $L_D^{\otimes m}$. Tensoring by a line bundle preserves exactness: on a trivializing open it is the identity functor. The closed-immersion projection formula [lem-pc-closed-immersion-coherent-cohomology] identifies $(i_*\mathcal O_D)\otimes L^{\otimes m}$ with $i_*L_D^{\otimes m}$. For the other sequence the canonical map $(p_*\mathcal O_E)\otimes L_D^{\otimes m}\to p_*(p^*L_D^{\otimes m})$ sends $b\otimes s$ to $b\,p^*s$; on a trivializing open it is the identity on $p_*\mathcal O_E$, so is an isomorphism, and these maps glue. By [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] the restriction of $p^*L_D^{\otimes m}$ to $E_i$ is $A_i^{\otimes m}$. Global sections on a finite disjoint union are the product by the sheaf axiom, equal to the finite direct sum. Thus the middle section map of this normalization sequence is the canonical map to $T_m:=\bigoplus_iT_{i,m}$.

source.place: Morphisms Tag 01QY (lemma-i-star-equivalence); Cohomology Tag 01E8 (lemma-projection-formula); modules.tex Tag 01CD (lemma-tensor-product-pullback). The finite-map projection calculation is written explicitly by local trivialization.

proof.text: The long exact derived-functor sequence [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] applies to global sections, whose derived functors are the module cohomology of [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. Using $H^1(X,J_m)=0$ and the closed-pushforward cohomology comparison of [lem-pc-closed-immersion-coherent-cohomology] gives $0\to H^0(X,J_m)\to H_m\xrightarrow{u_m}H^0(D,L_D^{\otimes m})\to0$. The normalization sequence gives $0\to H^0(D,L_D^{\otimes m})\xrightarrow{v_m}T_m\to H^0(D,Q_m)$. The composite $v_mu_m$ is $\rho_m$: each map restricts a section and then pulls it back along the indicated scheme morphism. Thus $\ker\rho_m=\ker u_m$ has dimension $a$, and surjectivity of $u_m$ identifies $\operatorname{coker}\rho_m$ with $\operatorname{coker}v_m$, a subspace of $H^0(D,Q_m)$; its dimension is at most $b$.

source.place: Tag 015B (lemma-higher-derived-functors), exact cohomology sequence; varieties.tex Tag 0AYT (lemma-chi-tensor-finite), vanishing from the preceding step.

proof.text: Every $H_m$ and $T_{i,m}$ is finite-dimensional for every $m\ge0$: the schemes are proper, their line bundles are coherent by [lem-trf-proper-field-invertible-coherent], and [lem-pc-euler-characteristic-well-defined] supplies finiteness. Put $g_i=\dim_kH^1(E_i,\mathcal O_{E_i})$, the genus [def-sc-genus]. By [lem-trf-curve-degree-tensor-additive], induction on $m$ gives $\deg A_i^{\otimes m}=me_i$ (degree of $\mathcal O_{E_i}$ is zero by its defining Euler difference). Choose $m_0=\max(0,\max_i(2g_i-1))$. Since $e_i$ is a positive integer, $m\ge m_0$ implies $me_i\ge2g_i-1$. The degree in [lem-sc-riemann-roch-large-degree] is that of [def-sc-pic0]; by [lem-sc-riemann-roch](1), applied to $A_i^{\otimes m}$ and to $\mathcal O_{E_i}$ (where $\chi(E_i,\mathcal O_{E_i})=1-g_i$), it equals $\chi(E_i,A_i^{\otimes m})-\chi(E_i,\mathcal O_{E_i})=me_i$. Therefore [lem-sc-riemann-roch-large-degree] gives $\dim_kT_{i,m}=me_i+1-g_i$.

source.place: Tag 0BS6 (lemma-rr), with large-degree Serre-duality vanishing as in the current blueprint lem-sc-riemann-roch-large-degree.proof.md; varieties.tex Tag 0AYX (lemma-degree-tensor-product).

proof.text: For a map of finite-dimensional spaces, a basis of its kernel extends to a basis of its source, whose remaining images form a basis of the image; extending the latter to a target basis gives $\dim H_m=\dim T_m+\dim\ker\rho_m-\dim\operatorname{coker}\rho_m$. Hence $|\dim H_m-\dim T_m|\le a+b$. Put $R=\sum_i|1-g_i|$ and $C=a+b+R$. The preceding step gives $|\dim T_{i,m}-me_i|=|1-g_i|\le R\le C$ and $|\dim T_m-m\sum_ie_i|=|\sum_i(1-g_i)|\le R$. The triangle inequality now gives $|\dim H_m-m\sum_ie_i|\le C$, while the kernel and cokernel bounds are $a\le C$ and $b\le C$. Both $C,m_0$ depend only on the given embedded scheme and are nonnegative integers, as required.
